absent: Full layout of the leading portion of TCP socket state preceding the routed tail and its initialization.
TCP loss recovery, congestion control, pacing, acknowledgment processing and timer callback behavior.
Trusted execution driver session management, invocation flow and shared memory lifecycle beyond accessors.
Terminal input conversion routines and architecture specific control character handling.
Architecture specific text patching synchronization and instruction cache maintenance.
Textsearch algorithm implementations, registration and concurrency control.
Thread information structure layout, flag numbering and architecture specific flag definitions.
Process identifier allocation and CPU count configuration enforcement.

findings.text: The trailing section of the TCP socket state collects connection management data in related groups. It holds a loss recovery marker, SYN and fast open indicators with repair queue and keepalive probe limits, AccECN failure and observation state, transmit delay, round trip deviation ceiling and reordering count, congestion window counters with clamp and use and stamp, recovery snapshots and delivered counts with out of window acknowledgment timing, pacing and compressed acknowledgment timers, cached out of order block, duplicate and selective acknowledgment storage with receive cache, loss onset and retransmission stamps with undo state, path MTU notification, retransmitted byte and packet totals with RTO count and time, urgent sequence with keepalive timing and linger, optional packet filter control, rehash timeouts, out of order packet count, MTU probe bounds, plus optional multipath, shared memory, authentication and fast open references.

SYN save uses two bits while related fast open and data flags use single bits, AccECN failure handling uses four bits with two bits for observation, and the packet filter change guard uses a single bit.

Duplicate acknowledgment storage holds one block while selective and receive cache each hold four, and duplicate plus selective are required to remain adjacent in memory because the options writing path treats them as a combined region.

Transmission queue throttling and queueing plus five deferred conditions form an ordered enumeration. Each flag value is a single bit selected by its enumeration position. The aggregate deferred mask combines the transmit queue deferred, write timer deferred, delayed acknowledgment deferred, MTU reduced deferred and pure acknowledgment deferred conditions, while excluding the throttled and queued indicators.

Helpers translate between a generic socket pointer and its enclosing TCP state in const preserving and mutable forms, and a separate helper reinterprets a generic socket pointer as timewait state. Callers use them to reach TCP specific fields from generic socket handling paths.

Timewait state extends the generic timewait base with receive window, timestamp offset and recent values with stamp, last out of window acknowledgment time, transmit delay, and optional message authentication references. Receive next and send next are aliases to fields in the shared common prefix rather than independent storage.
A socket counts as passively fast open only while in SYN received state and while its fast open request reference is present under RCU protection. Either condition alone is insufficient.
Queue tuning clamps a requested backlog against the network namespace connection limit and stores the smaller value as the fast open maximum queue length for the listener accept queue.

Saved SYN ownership moves from request to TCP socket by transferring the pointer and clearing the source, release frees the stored block and clears the holder, and length computation sums the recorded media, network and transport header lengths.

Maximum segment size clamping may run without holding the socket lock, notably on listeners, so it performs a single lockless load of the configured user limit and returns the smaller of that limit and the supplied estimate when a limit is set.
A destination query reports whether the route enables microsecond granularity TCP timestamps by testing its configured feature flag.

A trusted execution client context links its parent device with private driver data and a reference count, plus flags for release in progress, nonblocking supplicant behavior and null memory reference capability.

Shared memory is described by owning context, physical and kernel addresses, size, page offset, page array with count, reference count, flags, numeric identifier and secure world identifier. Parameters carry an attribute selector plus a variant payload that may be a shared memory reference with offset and size, an object reference with identifier and flags, a user buffer with address and size, or a triple value.
Small accessors expose the stored size, the page array with its count through an output argument, and the page offset without transferring ownership or altering reference counts.
A client device pairs an identifier with an embedded generic device. A client driver provides probe, remove and shutdown callbacks with an identifier table and an embedded generic driver.

Helpers convert between generic device or driver pointers and their enclosing trusted execution client structures, register a client driver against the current module, and expand module boilerplate to pair registration with unregistration.

Default control character assignments use interrupt as control C, quit as control backslash, erase as delete, kill as control U, end of file as control D, start as control Q, stop as control S, suspend as control Z, reprint as control R, discard as control O, word erase as control W, literal next as control V, with an optional suspend variant as control Y when that platform feature is enabled and omitted otherwise, and minimum count one.

The generic text patching fallback copies a byte range from source to destination with ordinary memory copy semantics and returns the destination pointer, with a marker definition signaling its presence.

Search state holds a current offset plus forty eight bytes of private scratch space. An algorithm operations table names the algorithm and supplies initialization, incremental search, teardown, pattern access, pattern length, owner and list linkage. A search configuration links its operations with flags plus callbacks to fetch the next data block and to finalize a sequence.

Starting a search resets the offset then advances once. Advancing invokes the algorithm find routine and then the optional finish callback before returning the match position. Pattern and pattern length getters delegate to the algorithm operations.

Private configuration storage is aligned to eight bytes. Allocation reserves aligned header space plus requested payload, zero fills it, reports out of memory through an error pointer on failure, and private access computes the address just past the aligned header.
Textsearch configuration flags define automatic module loading as value one and case insensitive matching as value two.

Finite state matching distinguishes specific character plus wildcard plus digit, hex digit, printable, alphabetic, alphanumeric, ascii, control, graphic, lower, upper, punctuation and space classes, with a maximum derived from the count. Recurrence distinguishes single, optional, zero or more, one or more and ignored leading repetitions, also with a derived maximum.
A finite state token packs a type selector, a recurrence selector and a literal value in four bytes.
The current thread information pointer is obtained by reinterpreting the current execution context pointer as thread information.
Stack address classification uses negative one for bad stack, zero for not stack, one for good frame and two for good stack in declaration order.

Each synchronous call work condition has a bit position and a corresponding single bit mask covering filtering, tracepoint, tracing, emulation, audit, user dispatch, exit trap and restartable sequence slicing in declaration order.

Lazy rescheduling aliases the standard rescheduling flag in both normal and mask forms, and restartable sequence handling aliases notify resume in both forms, so testing either name observes the same underlying bit.

Restart installation stores the supplied function in the restart block, invokes the architecture hook to record extra data, and returns the restart block error code. The generic architecture hook does nothing.
Thread stack alignment equals the thread size. Thread information allocation uses accounting with zeroing while skipping sanitizer poisoning.

Thread flags are modified through atomic bit operations on the flags word for set, clear, test and set, and test and clear, with conditional update selecting set or clear, while reads use a single lockless load. Variants exist for an explicit thread object, for the current thread and for task derived thread objects.

Synchronous call work has two storage configurations. One keeps a dedicated word in thread information for current and task variants of set, test and clear. The other reuses thread flag bits selected by matching thread flag names for the same operations.
Flag testing on the current thread has architecture specific and generic bit test variants, and the rescheduling query checks the standard rescheduling flag through that test.
The generic stack frame containment check always reports no containment, and the generic new execution setup performs no action.

Default CPU count is one when unconfigured and the active count follows configuration, with four threads reserved for root. Default identifier maximum is 4096 on small builds and 32768 otherwise. The absolute limit is eight times page size on small builds, otherwise 4194304 on wide word builds or the default on narrow builds. Per CPU defaults are 1024 with a minimum of 8.

Callers must handle allocation failure signaled through an error pointer rather than null, must not dereference the fast open request outside RCU protection, and must tolerate concurrent updates when reading user limits, connection limits, queue settings or thread flags through single loads and stores.
Context lifetime uses a kernel reference count with a releasing marker, while shared memory uses a separate reference count alongside identifiers for local and secure world handles.
A search progresses from reset to repeated block acquisition with incremental matching and ends with an optional finalization step that runs once per advance even when no further data remains.
The trusted execution client driver exposes probe for binding, remove for unbinding and shutdown for power transition as its interaction points with the driver core.
A textsearch algorithm exposes initialization, incremental find, destruction and pattern inspection as its interaction points with the generic search front end.
